clinician.trajectory_summary: A 10-month-old previously healthy infant presented with acute photophobia, eye blinking, irritability, and decreased oral intake. Ophthalmologic examination revealed bilateral dendritiform corneal lesions. Given maternal history of cold sores, herpetic keratitis was initially suspected. The infant responded to oral valacyclovir and Infectious Diseases recommended hospitalization for intravenous acyclovir. During admission, HSV PCR testing of a conjunctival swab and a papular crusted raised thumb lesion returned negative. Recognizing that dendritiform corneal lesions are characteristic of Tyrosinemia Type II, clinicians performed plasma amino acid chromatography, revealing markedly elevated plasma tyrosine (1262 µmol/L, reference range 40–80 µmol/L). The infant was placed on a tyrosine-restricted diet. After 2 weeks, plasma tyrosine decreased to 152 µmol/L (mildly elevated) and the corneal lesions had not recurred.
